DESIGN.md

show
## Concept
The player taps to toggle a dot between a tiny and a large form, using the tiny shape to slip through narrow gaps and the large shape to crush small obstacles. Timing the size change creates a rhythmic puzzle of fitting and smashing.

## Player
A single circular dot that travels forward through a scrolling tunnel. Visually it is a simple solid shape that can appear tiny or enlarged. Verb: toggle size (tap/click). The dot’s position is controlled automatically by the level flow; the player does not move it directly.

## Core loop
The game continuously scrolls forward, presenting a sequence of gaps and obstacles. Every few seconds a new challenge appears, and the player must decide whether to stay tiny to thread a narrow opening or grow large to smash a blocking block. The player reads the upcoming layout, taps to switch size, and watches the result unfold, repeating the decision rhythmically as the tunnel advances.

## Hazards / Obstacles
- **Narrow passages**: walls that leave only a slim corridor; the dot must be in its tiny form to pass safely.
- **Crushable blocks**: solid obstacles that block the path but are destroyed when the dot is large, clearing the way.
- **Static spikes**: deadly spikes that kill the dot regardless of size if collided with.
- **Moving sweepers**: horizontal bars that slide across the tunnel, requiring a timely size change to avoid contact.
- **Falling shards**: small pieces that descend; they are harmless to a large dot but can snag a tiny dot.

## Score
Score increases when the player:
- Successfully passes through a narrow passage.
- Crushes a block with the large form.
- Survives an entire wave of obstacles without dying.
Points are awarded per event, encouraging both precision and aggression.

## Win and lose
**Lose**: colliding with any obstacle while in an inappropriate size (e.g., hitting a narrow wall while large, or touching spikes in any form). On death the screen shows “Game Over”, the final score, and restart instructions.
**Win**: completing the final set of waves (or reaching a predefined score threshold) triggers a celebratory overlay with “You Win!” and the final tally.

## Feel
The game feels fast‑paced yet contemplative: a steady forward flow punctuated by quick, decisive size toggles. A neon‑lit aesthetic with high‑contrast cyan and magenta accents gives a retro‑futuristic vibe, while crisp chiptune blips punctuate each successful toggle, crush, or passage. The rhythm of toggling creates a satisfying loop of anticipation and payoff.

## Why it's fun
The moment you nail a perfect size switch—slipping through an impossible gap or pulverizing an obstacle in a single tap—delivers a burst of triumph that makes you grin, curse, and keep trying for the next perfect rhythm.

        // Clear background each frame
        const canvas = document.getElementById("game");
        const ctx = canvas.getContext("2d");
        ctx.fillStyle = "#0f1320";
        ctx.fillRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height);
        // Update player forward motion
        player.x += FORWARD_SPEED * dt;
        if (player.x > canvas.width) player.x = canvas.width; // clamp
        // Draw player
        const radius = player.size === "small" ? PLAYER_SMALL_RADIUS : PLAYER_LARGE_RADIUS;
        ctx.fillStyle = "#7df9ff";
        ctx.beginPath();
        ctx.arc(player.x, player.y, radius, 0, Math.PI * 2);
        ctx.fill();
        // Draw HUD (score)
        ctx.fillStyle = "#e6e6f0";
        ctx.font = "16px ui-sans-serif, system-ui";
        ctx.textAlign = "left";
        ctx.fillText(`Score ${score}`, 12, 22);
        // Update observable contract each frame
        window.__game.state = phase === "gameover" ? "gameover" : (phase === "menu" ? "menu" : "playing");
        window.__game.score = score;
        window.__game.player.x = player.x;
        window.__game.player.y = player.y;
        window.__game.player.visible = true;
        // Game‑over overlay
        if (phase === "gameover") {
          // Dim background
          ctx.fillStyle = "rgba(10,10,15,0.7)";
          ctx.fillRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height);
          // Game Over text
          ctx.textAlign = "center";
          ctx.font = "44px ui-sans-serif, system-ui";
          ctx.fillStyle = "#ff52ae";
          ctx.fillText("Game Over", canvas.width / 2, canvas.height / 2 - 20);
          // Final score
          ctx.font = "20px ui-sans-serif, system-ui";
          ctx.fillStyle = "#e6e6f0";
          ctx.fillText(`Final score ${score}`, canvas.width / 2, canvas.height / 2 + 14);
          // Restart instructions
          ctx.font = "16px ui-sans-serif, system-ui";
          ctx.fillStyle = "#a5a5b8";
          ctx.fillText("Press R or click Restart", canvas.width / 2, canvas.height / 2 + 42);
        }

      score = 0;

    let loopId = null;

    startLoop();

```html
    .game-header .game-controls { margin: 4px 0; padding-left: 18px; color: #c8c8d8; }
    main { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; padding: 16px; }
    canvas { background: #0f1320; border: 1px solid #2a2f44; }
    .game-restart { margin-top: 10px; padding: 8px 14px; background: #1c2030; color: #7df9ff; border: 1px solid #2a2f44; cursor: pointer; }
    .game-restart:hover { background: #232842; }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <header class="game-header">
    <h1>Neon Breaker</h1>
    <p class="game-description">Bounce the ball with the paddle and clear every brick. One ball, no second chances.</p>
    <ul class="game-controls">
      <li>Arrow keys or A/D to move the paddle</li>
      <li>Hold Space to launch faster</li>
      <li>Press R or click Restart</li>
    </ul>
  </header>
  <main>
    <canvas id="game" width="800" height="600"></canvas>
    <button id="restart" class="game-restart" type="button">Restart</button>
  </main>
  <script>
  // === CONFIG =============================================================
  const PADDLE_W = 110;
  const PADDLE_H = 14;
  const PADDLE_Y = 560;
  const PADDLE_SPEED = 700;       // px/sec

  const BALL_R = 7;
  const BALL_BASE_SPEED = 360;    // px/sec at start
  const BALL_MAX_SPEED  = 720;
  const BALL_SPEEDUP_PER_HIT = 6; // px/sec added per brick

  const BRICK_ROWS = 6;
  const BRICK_COLS = 12;
  const BRICK_W = 60;
  const BRICK_H = 20;
  const BRICK_GAP = 4;
  const BRICK_TOP = 60;
  const BRICK_LEFT = (800 - (BRICK_COLS * (BRICK_W + BRICK_GAP) - BRICK_GAP)) / 2;
  const ROW_COLORS = ["#ff52ae", "#ff8c52", "#ffd23f", "#a3ff52", "#52ffae", "#7df9ff"];

  // === STATE ==============================================================
  const canvas = document.getElementById("game");
  const ctx = canvas.getContext("2d");
  const restartBtn = document.getElementById("restart");

  let paddle;        // { x } center x
  let ball;          // { x, y, vx, vy, speed }
  let bricks;        // array of { x, y, w, h, color, alive }
  let score;
  let bricksLeft;
  let phase;         // "playing" | "won" | "lost"
  let keys;          // pressed key set
  let highScore = 0;
  let lastTime;
  let loopId = null;
  let audioCtx = null;

  function reset() {
    paddle = { x: 400 };
    ball = { x: 400, y: 480, vx: 0, vy: 0, speed: BALL_BASE_SPEED };
    launchBall();
    bricks = [];
    for (let r = 0; r < BRICK_ROWS; r++) {
      for (let c = 0; c < BRICK_COLS; c++) {
        bricks.push({
          x: BRICK_LEFT + c * (BRICK_W + BRICK_GAP),
          y: BRICK_TOP + r * (BRICK_H + BRICK_GAP),
          w: BRICK_W, h: BRICK_H,
          color: ROW_COLORS[r % ROW_COLORS.length],
          alive: true,
        });
      }
    }
    bricksLeft = bricks.length;
    score = 0;
    phase = "playing";
    keys = new Set();
    lastTime = performance.now();
    publishState();
    startLoop();
  }

  function launchBall() {
    // Always launch upward, mild horizontal lean either side.
    const angle = (-Math.PI / 2) + (Math.random() * 0.6 - 0.3);
    ball.vx = Math.cos(angle) * ball.speed;
    ball.vy = Math.sin(angle) * ball.speed;
  }

  function startLoop() {
    if (loopId !== null) cancelAnimationFrame(loopId);
    function tick(now) {
      try {
        const dt = Math.min((now - lastTime) / 1000, 0.1);
        lastTime = now;
        update(dt);
        render();
        publishState();
      } catch (err) {
        console.error("loop error", err);
      }
      loopId = requestAnimationFrame(tick);
    }
    loopId = requestAnimationFrame(tick);
  }

  // === UPDATE =============================================================
  function update(dt) {
    if (phase !== "playing") return;

    // Paddle.
    const dirX = (keys.has("ArrowRight") || keys.has("d") || keys.has("D") ? 1 : 0)
               - (keys.has("ArrowLeft")  || keys.has("a") || keys.has("A") ? 1 : 0);
    const speedMul = keys.has(" ") ? 1.6 : 1;
    paddle.x += dirX * PADDLE_SPEED * speedMul * dt;
    paddle.x = clamp(paddle.x, PADDLE_W / 2, canvas.width - PADDLE_W / 2);

    // Ball motion.
    ball.x += ball.vx * dt;
    ball.y += ball.vy * dt;

    // Walls.
    if (ball.x < BALL_R) { ball.x = BALL_R; ball.vx = Math.abs(ball.vx); beep(220, 0.04); }
    if (ball.x > canvas.width - BALL_R) { ball.x = canvas.width - BALL_R; ball.vx = -Math.abs(ball.vx); beep(220, 0.04); }
    if (ball.y < BALL_R) { ball.y = BALL_R; ball.vy = Math.abs(ball.vy); beep(220, 0.04); }

    // Floor — lose.
    if (ball.y > canvas.height + BALL_R) {
      phase = "lost";
      if (score > highScore) highScore = score;
      beep(110, 0.25);
      return;
    }

    // Paddle.
    const px = paddle.x, py = PADDLE_Y;
    if (ball.vy > 0
        && ball.y + BALL_R >= py
        && ball.y - BALL_R <= py + PADDLE_H
        && ball.x >= px - PADDLE_W / 2 - BALL_R
        && ball.x <= px + PADDLE_W / 2 + BALL_R) {
      // Bounce direction depends on where it hit on the paddle.
      const offset = (ball.x - px) / (PADDLE_W / 2); // -1..1
      const angle = (-Math.PI / 2) + offset * 1.0;   // up-ish, leaning side
      ball.vx = Math.cos(angle) * ball.speed;
      ball.vy = Math.sin(angle) * ball.speed;
      ball.y = py - BALL_R - 0.1;
      beep(540, 0.05);
    }

    // Bricks.
    for (const b of bricks) {
      if (!b.alive) continue;
      if (ball.x + BALL_R < b.x || ball.x - BALL_R > b.x + b.w) continue;
      if (ball.y + BALL_R < b.y || ball.y - BALL_R > b.y + b.h) continue;

      b.alive = false;
      bricksLeft--;
      score += 10;
      ball.speed = Math.min(BALL_MAX_SPEED, ball.speed + BALL_SPEEDUP_PER_HIT);

      // Decide which side was hit by comparing penetrations.
      const overlapX = Math.min(ball.x + BALL_R - b.x, b.x + b.w - (ball.x - BALL_R));
      const overlapY = Math.min(ball.y + BALL_R - b.y, b.y + b.h - (ball.y - BALL_R));
      if (overlapX < overlapY) ball.vx = -ball.vx; else ball.vy = -ball.vy;

      // Renormalize to current speed.
      const m = Math.hypot(ball.vx, ball.vy);
      ball.vx = (ball.vx / m) * ball.speed;
      ball.vy = (ball.vy / m) * ball.speed;
      beep(880, 0.05);
      break;
    }

    if (bricksLeft === 0) {
      phase = "won";
      if (score > highScore) highScore = score;
      beep(990, 0.2);
    }
  }

  // === RENDER =============================================================
  function render() {
    ctx.fillStyle = "#0f1320";
    ctx.fillRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height);

    // Bricks.
    for (const b of bricks) {
      if (!b.alive) continue;
      ctx.fillStyle = b.color;
      ctx.fillRect(b.x, b.y, b.w, b.h);
    }

    // Paddle.
    ctx.fillStyle = "#7df9ff";
    ctx.fillRect(paddle.x - PADDLE_W / 2, PADDLE_Y, PADDLE_W, PADDLE_H);

    // Ball.
    ctx.fillStyle = "#ffffff";
    ctx.beginPath();
    ctx.arc(ball.x, ball.y, BALL_R, 0, Math.PI * 2);
    ctx.fill();

    // HUD.
    ctx.fillStyle = "#e6e6f0";
    ctx.font = "16px ui-sans-serif, system-ui";
    ctx.textAlign = "left";
    ctx.fillText(`Score ${score}`, 12, 22);
    ctx.textAlign = "right";
    ctx.fillText(`Bricks ${bricksLeft}  ·  Best ${highScore}`, canvas.width - 12, 22);

    if (phase === "lost" || phase === "won") {
      ctx.fillStyle = "rgba(10,10,15,0.7)";
      ctx.fillRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height);
      ctx.textAlign = "center";
      ctx.font = "44px ui-sans-serif, system-ui";
      ctx.fillStyle = phase === "won" ? "#52ffae" : "#ff52ae";
      ctx.fillText(phase === "won" ? "You Win!" : "Game Over", canvas.width / 2, canvas.height / 2 - 20);
      ctx.fillStyle = "#e6e6f0";
      ctx.font = "20px ui-sans-serif, system-ui";
      ctx.fillText(`Final score ${score}`, canvas.width / 2, canvas.height / 2 + 14);
      ctx.fillStyle = "#a5a5b8";
      ctx.font = "16px ui-sans-serif, system-ui";
      ctx.fillText("Press R or click Restart", canvas.width / 2, canvas.height / 2 + 42);
    }
  }

  // === INPUT ==============================================================
  document.addEventListener("keydown", (ev) => {
    if (ev.key === "r" || ev.key === "R") { reset(); return; }
    keys.add(ev.key);
  });
  document.addEventListener("keyup", (ev) => { keys.delete(ev.key); });
  restartBtn.addEventListener("click", reset);

  // === AUDIO (lazy) =======================================================
  function beep(freq, durSec) {
    try {
      if (!audioCtx) audioCtx = new (window.AudioContext || window.webkitAudioContext)();
      const osc = audioCtx.createOscillator();
      const gain = audioCtx.createGain();
      osc.type = "square";
      osc.frequency.value = freq;
      gain.gain.setValueAtTime(0.05, audioCtx.currentTime);
      gain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.001, audioCtx.currentTime + durSec);
      osc.connect(gain); gain.connect(audioCtx.destination);
      osc.start(); osc.stop(audioCtx.currentTime + durSec);
    } catch {}
  }

  // === OBSERVABLE CONTRACT ===============================================
  function publishState() {
    window.__game = {
      state: phase === "playing" ? "playing" : "gameover",
      score,
      player: {
        x: paddle.x,
        y: PADDLE_Y + PADDLE_H / 2,
        visible: paddle.x >= 0 && paddle.x <= canvas.width,
      },
      objective: "Bounce the ball with the paddle to break every brick.",
    };
  }

  // === HELPERS ============================================================
  function clamp(v, lo, hi) { return v < lo ? lo : (v > hi ? hi : v); }

  // === BOOT ===============================================================
  reset();
  </script>
</body>
</html>
```

Stay alive as long as you can.\",\n24:   \"controls\": [\"Arrow keys to move\", \"Space to fire\"],\n25:   \"tags\": [\"arcade\", \"dodge\"]\n26: }\n27: ```\n28: \n29: Rules:\n30: - `title` — string, 3–80 characters, matches the game's display name.\n31: - `description` — string, 20–400 characters, one short paragraph.\n32: - `controls` — non-empty array of short strings, one per control.\n33: - `tags` — optional array of lowercase keywords.\n34: \n35: ## `index.html` requirements\n36: \n37: ### Self-contained\n38: - All CSS goes in a single `<style>` block in `<head>`.\n39: - All JS goes in a single `<script>` block at the end of `<body>`.\n40: - **No** external resources: no `<script src=\"https://...\">`, no `<link href=\"https://...\">`, no `<img src=\"https://...\">`, no CDN imports.\n41: - **No** network calls at runtime: no `fetch`, no `XMLHttpRequest`, no `import()`, no `WebSocket`.\n42: \n43: ### Required structure (in this order)\n44: \n45: ```html\n46: <!DOCTYPE html>\n47: <html lang=\"en\">\n48: <head>\n49:   <meta charset=\"utf-8\">\n50:   <title>YOUR TITLE</title>\n51:   <style>/* inline only */</style>\n52: </head>\n53: <body>\n54:   <header class=\"game-header\">\n55:     <h1>YOUR TITLE</h1>\n56:     <p class=\"game-description\">YOUR DESCRIPTION</p>\n57:     <ul class=\"game-controls\">\n58:       <li>YOUR CONTROL</li>\n59:     </ul>\n60:   </header>\n61:   <main>\n62:     <canvas id=\"game\" width=\"800\" height=\"600\"></canvas>\n63:     <button id=\"restart\" class=\"game-restart\" type=\"button\">Restart</button>\n64:   </main>\n65:   <script>/* inline only */</script>\n66: </body>\n67: </html>\n68: ```\n69: \n70: - Exactly one `<canvas id=\"game\">` (you may set width/height to other values; 800x600 is recommended).\n71: - Exactly one `<button id=\"restart\" class=\"game-restart\">` immediately after the canvas. Clicking it must fully reset the game (same code path as the R key). It must be visible and clickable at all times — not only on game-over.\n72: - The `<header>`'s `<h1>` text must match `meta.json.title` exactly.\n73: - The `<p class=\"game-description\">` text must match `meta.json.description` exactly.\n74: - The `<li>` items in `<ul class=\"game-controls\">` must match `meta.json.controls` in order.\n75: \n76: ### Behavior\n77: - The game must start rendering immediately on page load (no \"click to start\" required).\n78: - Use keyboard and/or mouse input.\n79: - The script must not throw any uncaught exception in the first 5 seconds.\n80: - If you use `localStorage` or `sessionStorage`, all keys must start with the prefix `slop-factory:size-shift-2:`.\n81: \n82: ### Style\n83: - Dark background (the gallery is dark — recommend `#0a0a0f` or similar).\n84: - High-contrast neon accents (e.g. cyan `#7df9ff`, magenta `#ff00aa`, yellow `#ffd23f`).\n85: - The `<header>` is shown above the canvas — keep its styling minimal and let the canvas content shine.\n86: \n87: ## What makes a tiny canvas game feel good\n88: \n89: Aim for these qualities in every game you produce:\n90: \n91: 1. **Immediate input response** — every keystroke or click produces visible action within one frame. Never make the player wait.\n92: 2. **Clear feedback** — the player always knows when something happened. Use color flashes, particles, brief screen shake, score popups, or sound on every meaningful event (hit, score, miss, death).\n93: 3. **Win/lose state** — the game has a clear end condition. On lose, draw \"Game Over\" + final score + restart instructions on the canvas. On restart you MUST `cancelAnimationFrame` any pending loop before starting a new one (otherwise loops stack on each restart and the game eventually slows to a crawl).\n95: 5. **Progressive difficulty** — start gentle so the player can learn, then ramp up. Don't dump them into chaos at t=0.\n96: 6. **No dead time** — something interesting on screen at all times. A game that violates any of these is broken even if it runs without errors. After your implementation finishes, the validator loads the page in a real browser and runs an 8-second playtest with synthetic input — failures here are reported back to you and must be fixed before the game ships.\n103: \n104: ### 1. The player can lose\n105: \n106: There must be a collision check (or other end condition) that fires `gameOver` and stops the active gameplay loop. \"Game runs forever, no death\" is broken. Examples that have failed in the past: collision check compared a value against itself; \"spike\" collision only clamped position instead of killing the player; obstacles never reached the player.\n107: \n108: ### 2. The player can score\n109: \n110: The score must increase on a **discrete event** (a survived obstacle, a collected pickup, an enemy destroyed, a beat hit). \"Score = elapsed seconds\" is allowed but weak. Score must be drawn on the canvas at all times.\n111: \n112: ### 3. The first 3 seconds are survivable with no input\n113: \n114: Define a `SAFE_RADIUS` (e.g. 200px) around the player's starting position. When spawning hazards, **reject any spawn that is within `SAFE_RADIUS` of the player AND would reach them within 3 seconds at current hazard speed**. Pre-spawning hazards on top of the player at t=0 has caused frame-1 deaths in past games. Don't do it.\n115: \n116: ### 4. The control actually changes the outcome\n117: \n118: Whatever the player presses must, in the next frame, change a value that affects collision or score. If a control is purely cosmetic (e.g. \"stretch horizontally\" but the gaps are vertical), the game is fundamentally broken even if it runs. After writing, **re-read the game's concept and trace one frame**: does the input do what the concept claims?\n119: \n120: ### 5. dt-based physics, not per-frame constants\n121: \n122: All movement and timing must scale by delta time (seconds since last frame). Per-frame constants (`x += 5` every frame) make games run 2.4× faster on a 144Hz display.\n123: \n124: ```js\n125: let lastTime = performance.now();\n126: function loop(now) {\n127:   const dt = Math.min((now - lastTime) / 1000, 0.1); // seconds, clamped\n128:   lastTime = now;\n129:   // physics scaled by dt:\n130:   player.x += player.vx * dt;\n131:   enemy.y  += enemy.vy  * dt;\n132:   spawnTimer -= dt;\n133:   // ...\n134:   requestAnimationFrame(loop);\n135: }\n136: requestAnimationFrame(loop);\n137: ```\n138: \n139: ### 6. Restart fully resets AND cancels the prior loop\n140: \n141: Both R and the Restart button must call the same reset function. That function MUST `cancelAnimationFrame(loopId)` the previous loop before scheduling a new one — otherwise loops stack on each restart and the game slows to a crawl over time.\n142: \n143: ```js\n144: let loopId = null;\n145: function startLoop() {\n146:   if (loopId !== null) cancelAnimationFrame(loopId);\n147:   function tick(now) { /* ... */ loopId = requestAnimationFrame(tick); }\n148:   loopId = requestAnimationFrame(tick);\n149: }\n150: ```\n151: \n152: ### 7. Game-over overlay shows score and restart instructions\n153: \n154: When the player dies, draw on the canvas: \"Game Over\", final score, current high score (if you persist one), and \"Press R or click Restart\". A game that does not expose this object is rejected.\n159: \n160: ```js\n161: window.__game = {\n162:   state: \"menu\",        // \"menu\" | \"playing\" | \"gameover\" — exact strings, no others\n163:   score: 0,             // current score, number\n164:   player: {\n165:     x: 400,             // player x in canvas coordinates (0 = left)\n166:     y: 300,             // player y in canvas coordinates (0 = top)\n167:     visible: true,      // true if the player is currently rendered inside the canvas viewport\n168:   },\n169:   objective: \"Dodge falling neon blocks. Survive as long as possible.\", // 10-200 chars, one sentence\n170: };\n171: ```\n172: \n173: Rules:\n174: - The object must exist from the very first frame, before any input.\n175: - Update `state`, `score`, `player.x`, `player.y`, and `player.visible` whenever they change. The simplest approach is to update them at the end of your render/update step each frame.\n176: - `state` must only ever be one of the three exact strings.     // Canvas and rendering context

```
<script>
    // Placeholder script for Size Shift game. Actual game logic will be added in later tasks.
    // === STATE ==============================================================
    // Game state objects
    const player = { x: 400, y: 300, size: "small", visible: true };
    const hazards = []; // array of obstacle objects
    let score = 0;
    let phase = "menu"; // "menu" | "playing" | "gameover"
    // Ensures the page loads without errors.
    // === INPUT ==============================================================
    const keys = new Set();
    function reset() {
        // Reset game state to initial values
        player.x = 400;
        player.y = 300;
        player.size = "small";
        player.visible = true;
        hazards.length = 0;
        score = 0;
        phase = "menu";
        // Update observable state
        window.__game.state = "menu";
        window.__game.score = 0;
        window.__game.player.x = player.x;
        window.__game.player.y = player.y;
        window.__game.player.visible = player.visible;
    }
    document.addEventListener("keydown", (ev) => {
        if (ev.key === "r" || ev.key === "R") { reset(); return; }
        keys.add(ev.key);
    });
    document.addEventListener("keyup", (ev) => {
        keys.delete(ev.key);
    });
    const restartBtn = document.getElementById("restart");
    restartBtn.addEventListener("click", reset);
    window.__game = {
      state: "menu",
      score: 0,
      player: { x: 400, y: 300, visible: true },
      objective: "Tap to toggle size and survive the tunnel obstacles."
    };
</script>
```

```
<script>
    // Placeholder script for Size Shift game. Actual game logic will be added in later tasks.
    // === STATE ==============================================================
    // Game state objects
    const player = { x: 400, y: 300, size: "small", visible: true };
    const hazards = []; // array of obstacle objects
    const FORWARD_SPEED = 150; // forward speed in px/sec
    const LATERAL_SPEED = 300; // lateral speed in px/sec
    let phase = "menu"; // "menu" | "playing" | "gameover"
    // Ensures the page loads without errors.
    // === INPUT ==============================================================
    const keys = new Set();
    function reset() {
        // Reset game state to initial values
        player.x = 400;
        player.y = 300;
        player.size = "small";
        player.visible = true;
        hazards.length = 0;
        score = 0;
        phase = "menu";
        // Update observable state
        window.__game.state = "menu";
        window.__game.score = 0;
        window.__game.player.x = player.x;
        window.__game.player.y = player.y;
        window.__game.player.visible = player.visible;
    }
    document.addEventListener("keydown", (ev) => {
        if (ev.key === "r" || ev.key === "R") { reset(); return; }
        keys.add(ev.key);
    });
    document.addEventListener("keyup", (ev) => {
        keys.delete(ev.key);
    });
    const restartBtn = document.getElementById("restart");
    restartBtn.addEventListener("click", reset);
    // Size toggle on canvas click / tap
    function toggleSize() {
        player.size = (player.size === "small") ? "large" : "small";
    }
    document.getElementById("game").addEventListener("click", toggleSize);
    // === LOOP ==============================================================
    let loopId = null;
    let lastTime = performance.now();
    function startLoop() {
        if (loopId !== null) cancelAnimationFrame(loopId);
        function tick(now) {
            try {
                const dt = Math.min((now - lastTime) / 1000, 0.1);
                lastTime = now;
                // placeholder: clear canvas each frame
                const canvas = document.getElementById("game");
                const ctx = canvas.getContext("2d");
                ctx.fillStyle = "#0f1320";
                ctx.fillRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height);
            } catch (err) {
                console.error("loop error", err);
            }
            loopId = requestAnimationFrame(tick);
        }
        loopId = requestAnimationFrame(tick);
    }
    // Start animation loop
    startLoop();
    
    window.__game = {
      state: "menu",
      score: 0,
      player: { x: 400, y: 300, visible: true },
      objective: "Tap to toggle size and survive the tunnel obstacles."
    };
</script>
```

```
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  ... style ...
</head>
<body>
  <header ...> ...
  <main>
    <canvas id="game" width="800" height="600"></canvas>
    <button id="restart" class="game-restart" type="button">Restart</button>
  </main>
  <script>
    // Placeholder script for Size Shift game. Actual game logic will be added in later tasks.
    // === STATE ==============================================================
    // Game state objects
    const player = { x: 400, y: 300, size: "small", visible: true };
    const hazards = []; // array of obstacle objects
    const FORWARD_SPEED = 150; // forward speed in px/sec
    const LATERAL_SPEED = 300; // lateral speed in px/sec
    let score = 0;
    let phase = "menu"; // "menu" | "playing" | "gameover"
    // Ensures the page loads without errors.
    // === INPUT ==============================================================
    const keys = new Set();
    function reset() {
        // Reset game state to initial values
        player.x = 400;
        player.y = 300;
        player.size = "small";
        player.visible = true;
        hazards.length = 0;
        score = 0;
        phase = "menu";
        // Update observable state
        window.__game.state = "menu";
        window.__game.score = 0;
        window.__game.player.x = player.x;
        window.__game.player.y = player.y;
        window.__game.player.visible = player.visible;
    }
    document.addEventListener("keydown", (ev) => {
        if (ev.key === "r" || ev.key === "R") { reset(); return; }
        keys.add(ev.key);
    });
    document.addEventListener("keyup", (ev) => {
        keys.delete(ev.key);
    });
    const restartBtn = document.getElementById("restart");
    restartBtn.addEventListener("click", reset);
    // Size toggle on canvas click / tap
    function toggleSize() {
        player.size = (player.size === "small") ? "large" : "small";
    }
    document.getElementById("game").addEventListener("click", toggleSize);
    // === LOOP ==============================================================
    let loopId = null;
    let lastTime = performance.now();
    function startLoop() {
        if (loopId !== null) cancelAnimationFrame(loopId);
        function tick(now) {
            try {
                const dt = Math.min((now - lastTime) / 1000, 0.1);
                lastTime = now;
                // placeholder: clear canvas each frame
                const canvas = document.getElementById("game");
                const ctx = canvas.getContext("2d");
                ctx.fillStyle = "#0f1320";
                ctx.fillRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height);
            } catch (err) {
                console.error("loop error", err);
            }
            loopId = requestAnimationFrame(tick);
        }
        loopId = requestAnimationFrame(tick);
    }
    // Start animation loop
    startLoop();
    
    window.__game = {
      state: "menu",
      score: 0,
      player: { x: 400, y: 300, visible: true },
      objective: "Tap to toggle size and survive the tunnel obstacles."
    };
  </script>
</body>
</html>
```

Add constants:

```
const SAFE_RADIUS = 100; // pixels
const SPAWN_INTERVAL = 2; // seconds
let spawnTimer = 0;
```

Add functions:

```
function update(dt) {
    if (phase !== "playing") return;
    
    // Player forward motion (auto forward)
    player.y -= FORWARD_SPEED * dt;
    // optional lateral drift from keys
    const dirX = (keys.has("ArrowRight") || keys.has("d") || keys.has("D") ? 1 : 0) -
                 (keys.has("ArrowLeft") || keys.has("a") || keys.has("A") ? 1 : 0);
    player.x += dirX * LATERAL_SPEED * dt;

    // Keep player within canvas bounds
    player.x = clamp(player.x, PLAYER_LARGE_RADIUS, canvas.width - PLAYER_LARGE_RADIUS);
    player.y = clamp(player.y, PLAYER_SMALL_RADIUS, canvas.height - PLAYER_SMALL_RADIUS);
    
    // Spawn hazards
    spawnTimer -= dt;
    if (spawnTimer <= 0) {
        spawnTimer = SPAWN_INTERVAL;
        const hazard = {
            x: Math.random() * (canvas.width - 20) + 10,
            y: canvas.height + 20,
            radius: 12,
            // Could have type but not needed
        };
        // Ensure not within SAFE_RADIUS of player
        const dx = hazard.x - player.x;
        const dy = hazard.y - player.y;
        if (Math.hypot(dx, dy) > SAFE_RADIUS) {
            hazards.push(hazard);
        }
    }

    // Move hazards toward player (upward)
    for (let i = hazards.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
        const h = hazards[i];
        h.y -= FORWARD_SPEED * dt;
        // Check collision with player
        const playerRadius = (player.size === "small") ? PLAYER_SMALL_RADIUS : PLAYER_LARGE_RADIUS;
        if (Math.hypot(h.x - player.x, h.y - player.y) < playerRadius + h.radius) {
            phase = "gameover";
            // Update observable state later
            break;
        }
        // Remove hazards that passed beyond top
        if (h.y + h.radius < 0) {
            hazards.splice(i, 1);
            score += 10; // scoring for survived hazard
        }
    }

    // Increment score over time as a fallback (optional)
    // score += dt * 1; // not necessary
}
```

```
function render() {
    // background already cleared
    // draw hazards
    ctx.fillStyle = "#ff52ae";
    for (const h of hazards) {
        ctx.beginPath();
        ctx.arc(h.x, h.y, h.radius, 0, Math.PI * 2);
        ctx.fill();
    }

    // draw player
    ctx.fillStyle = player.size === "small" ? "#7df9ff" : "#ff00aa";
    const radius = player.size === "small" ? PLAYER_SMALL_RADIUS : PLAYER_LARGE_RADIUS;
    ctx.beginPath();
    ctx.arc(player.x, player.y, radius, 0, Math.PI * 2);
    ctx.fill();

    // HUD
    ctx.fillStyle = "#e6e6f0";
    ctx.font = "16px ui-sans-serif, system-ui";
    ctx.textAlign = "left";
    ctx.fillText(`Score ${Math.floor(score)}`, 12, 22);
}
```

Pseudo:

let audioCtx = null;
function beep(freq, durSec) {
  try {
    if (!audioCtx) audioCtx = new (window.AudioContext || window.webkitAudioContext)();
    const osc = audioCtx.createOscillator();
    const gain = audioCtx.createGain();
    osc.type = "square";
    osc.frequency.value = freq;
    gain.gain.setValueAtTime(0.05, audioCtx.currentTime);
    gain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.001, audioCtx.currentTime + durSec);
    osc.connect(gain);
    gain.connect(audioCtx.destination);
    osc.start();
    osc.stop(audioCtx.currentTime + durSec);
  } catch {}
}

prompt (5,181 chars)
Read CONVENTIONS.md and DESIGN.md in your working directory before doing anything else.

Your job in this stage is to break the implementation into a numbered list of small, ordered tasks. The next stage will work through this list one task at a time, in a single LLM session, reloading the page after each task and capturing console errors for you to fix.

Title: Size Shift
Concept: Tap to toggle the dot between a small and a large size; the tiny form slips through narrow gaps while the large form covers broader openings and can crush small obstacles, forcing you to switch sizes at the right moments.

**You must produce one output file: `TASKS.md` in the working directory.** Use your write/edit tool to create this file on disk. After your turn ends, the validator runs `readFile("TASKS.md")` — if the file does not exist on disk, validation fails and your work is wasted. **Do NOT reply with the task list as inline chat text.** The list must be written to the file.

**Tool calls MUST be emitted as actual function/tool invocations — NOT described or simulated inside your reasoning/analysis text.** Writing tool-shaped JSON like `{"filePath":"TASKS.md","content":"..."}` *inside your chain-of-thought* does NOT invoke any tool. It is just text in the analysis channel that nothing reads or executes. The same goes for `{"pattern":"**/*"}` etc. — those only do something when emitted as a real `tool_use` event from the action channel, never when written into your thinking. Several prior runs have failed by hallucinating tool calls inside reasoning; do not repeat that pattern. If at any point you "describe" a tool call in your thinking instead of invoking it, you must immediately invoke the real tool afterward. The format MUST be a numbered list, one task per line, each line starting with `<number>.`:

```
1. <Task title> — <one-sentence description of what to do>
2. <Task title> — <one-sentence description>
...
```

The next stage parses tasks by matching `^\d+\.` at the start of each line. Don't use bullet sub-lists, don't number sub-tasks (1.1, 1.2). One number, one task, one line.

### What makes a good task

- **Small enough** to complete in a single coding turn (~50–150 lines of edits).
- **Testable**: after this task, what does the page do that it didn't before?
- **Leaves the file runnable**: at the end of the task, no syntax errors, no uncaught exceptions on load. Even if the game isn't playable yet, it must load.
- **Specific**: don't say "implement player". Say "implement player movement: arrow keys set keys.left/right; in update(), apply acceleration in the pressed direction with cap at MAX_SPEED, friction otherwise; clamp x to canvas bounds."
- **Concrete numbers**: this is where pixel sizes, ms intervals, and px/sec speeds live. Pick them. The implement stage will use them verbatim.

### Required coverage (in roughly this order)

Cover at minimum, ordered as below. Add tasks if the design demands more (powerups, level progression, screen wrap, etc):

1. **HTML scaffold + meta.json**: header (h1, description, controls list), canvas, restart button per CONVENTIONS.md. Stub `<script>` block (empty). meta.json matching header text.
2. **Game state objects**: player, hazards, score, phase using plain object literals at the top of the script. Set initial values.
3. **requestAnimationFrame loop**: startLoop() with `cancelAnimationFrame(loopId)` discipline at the top. Body wrapped in try/catch. Calls update(dt) and render(). Don't draw anything yet besides clearing the canvas.
4. **Input**: a `keys` Set populated by document keydown/keyup. R-key restart hook. Restart button click hook. Both call the same reset() function.
5. **Player movement**: dt-based physics tied to the key inputs from task 4. Verify each control listed in meta.json actually changes a value.
6. **Hazards**: data structure, spawn rules with a SAFE_RADIUS so nothing spawns on top of the player at t=0, motion (dt-scaled).
7. **Collision detection**: player vs hazards. On hit, transition phase to "gameover" and stop the active gameplay.
8. **Score**: discrete events that increase score, drawn on canvas at top-left.
9. **Render**: clear canvas, draw background, hazards, player, HUD. Player must be the highest-contrast object on screen.
10. **Game-over overlay**: dim background, "Game Over", final score, "Press R or click Restart".
11. **Observable contract**: populate `window.__game = { state, score, player:{x,y,visible}, objective }` every frame. `state` is "playing" | "gameover". `objective` is a 10–200 char single-sentence description.
12. **Audio**: lazy-init AudioContext inside a beep() helper, wrapped in try/catch. Hook into hit / score / death events.

You may merge two trivial tasks if they truly belong together (e.g. tasks 1+2 if state is just three lines). You may split a complex task in two. Aim for 10–15 tasks total.

**Final check before you stop**: confirm you actually called your write/edit tool with `TASKS.md` as the path. If you only described the task list in chat without invoking the tool, the file will not exist on disk and validation will fail. After the file is written, stop. Do not begin implementation.
